annotationRationale: Both methods prove a lower bound and exhibit a strategy attaining it. The first uses disjoint candidates; the alternative bounds how many positions guesses eliminate. Neither requires formal graph terminology.

review.questionCheck: Four turns are necessary and sufficient, giving choice C. The supplied shared AMC 12B Q05 record agrees. The grid is fully specified in words, so no missing figure creates a conflict.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The retained packing and position-counting arguments give genuinely different lower bounds. The nonadjacent-cell formulation does not warrant an additional route here.
review.annotationCheck: Discrete extremal bounds and constructions is the exact assessed skill. Neither formal graph terminology nor the supplied pigeonhole node is required by these explanations.

methodReviews.mathCheck: All four listed pairs are legal, mutually disjoint rectangle positions. Three guesses can touch at most three pairs. An untouched pair is consistent with the entire adaptive all-miss branch. Conversely, every legal rectangle contains exactly one of squares 2,4,6,8, proving the minimum is 4.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The checkerboard construction matches LIVE and AoPS Solution 4. The disjoint-placement lower bound is honestly distinguished from those source strategies and is consistent with the supplied existing packing route. Source-informed-original is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The numbered grid makes the packing explicit, and the all-miss explanation resolves the adaptive-strategy difficulty. The coloring argument is accessible without an additional diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:extremal-principle directly matches the universal lower bound together with an attaining four-guess construction.

methodReviews.mathCheck: There are 6 horizontal and 6 vertical positions. Without a center guess, three guesses meet at most 9 positions. With the center guessed, its 4 positions plus at most 2 for each other guess total at most 8. Thus an all-miss branch remains possible. The four side-middle squares meet every position, establishing 4.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: This accurately follows AoPS Solution 1's position count and center split, using original prose and explicitly handling adaptive guesses. It makes no official-MAA attribution.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first move explains why position coverage matters. Removing center-containing positions leaves only perimeter adjacencies, making the two-partner bound understandable. The upper bound independently completes the solution.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:extremal-principle is directly demonstrated by a universal impossibility bound and a matching feasible strategy.
